An agenda of such special meeting is attached hereto incorporated herein by reference and
made a part hereof as though fully set forth herein.

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M25-34

The City Clerk hereby reports that she duly gave notice of the Special Meeting of the City
Council being held this morning pursuant to the order of the Mayor and in accordance with
Section 54956 of the Government Code of the State of California.

1.  CITY COUNCIL STRATEGIC PLANNING SESSION – F2M25-28

  The City Council, City Manager, Department Heads and Facilitator William Kelly,
  President/CEO of Kelly Associates Management Group, held a strategic planning
  session on March 4, 2025 to update the City’s Strategic Plan adopted in 2024. The Draft
  Strategic Plan contains six Goals, defined as follows: Goal 1: Enhance Public Safety;
  Goal 2: Improve Infrastructure and Mobility; Goal 3: Create a Strong Financial Base and
  Strong Economic Base (Economic Development); Goal 4: Enhance Transparency and

  2
3-13-25
   Open Governance; Goal 5: Promote Sustainability; and, Goal 6: Improve Housing
  Opportunities, and an Implementation Plan to provide details and metrics to monitor the
  Plan. The City Council will review and discuss the Draft Strategic Plan.

  Recommended Action:  City Council review the 2025 City of Alhambra Draft
  Strategic Plan and direct staff as deemed appropriate.

ADJOURNMENT: The next regularly scheduled meeting of the Alhambra City Council will be
held on Monday, March 24, 2025, in the Alhambra City Hall Council Chambers, 111 South First
Street, Alhambra, California, commencing at 6:00 p.m.

  NOTICE
Agenda Items: Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to the items listed
on this agenda are on file with the City Clerk in Alhambra City Hall, located at 111 South First Street,
Alhambra, California, and are available for inspection during regular office hours, Monday through
Thursday from 7:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. If you would like to sign-up to receive the City Council meeting
agenda and staff reports packet, please visit the City’s website at www.cityofalhambra.org and you
will be able to submit your email address on the homepage to the subscription service. Pursuant to
Government Code Section 54957.5(b), materials related to agenda items for regular meetings of the
Alhambra City Council that are distributed less than 72 hours prior to that meeting, will be made
available for public inspection at the Alhambra City Clerk’s Office.

Americans with Disabilities Act: If you require special assistance to participate in any City
meeting (including assisted listening devices), please contact the City Clerk's Office at (626) 570-
5090. Notification of at least 72 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable
arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting.

Translation Services Requests: If you require translation services in order to participate in a
meeting please contact the City Clerk’s Office at (626) 570-5090. All requests for translation services
shall be made by 4 p.m. the Thursday prior to the City Council meeting. If translation is not
requested by 4 p.m. the Thursday prior to the City Council meeting, staff will try to accommodate the
request if possible.

  LAUREN MYLES, CMC
  CITY CLERK

  MINUTES
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  Special Meeting
  March 13, 2025
  10:00 a.m.

ROLL CALL: At 10:08 a.m., on Thursday, March 13, 2025, the Alhambra City Council met in Ruth
Reese Hall of the Alhambra Civic Center Library, 101 South First Street, Alhambra, California.

CITY COUNCIL:  PRESENT:  MAZA, MALONEY, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE
  ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Stover, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks & Recreation Macias, Director of
Library Services LohGuan, Director of Public Works/Utilities Ray, Director of Finance Lieu, Director of
Human Resources Ko, Director of Community Development Ho, Fire Chief Ragusa, Chief of Police
Kennedy, Deputy Director of Public Works/Utilities Ahlen, Manager Analyst Alvarez

Also present was Facilitator William R. Kelly, President/CEO of Kelly Associates Management Group

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M25-34

The City Clerk hereby reported that she duly gave notice of the Special Meeting of the City Council
being held this morning pursuant to the order of the Mayor and in accordance with Section 54956 of
the Government Code of the State of California.

1.  CITY COUNCIL STRATEGIC PLANNING SESSION – F2M25-28

  The City Council, City Manager, Department Heads and Facilitator William Kelly,
  President/CEO of Kelly Associates Management Group, held a strategic planning session on
  March 4, 2025 to update the City’s Strategic Plan adopted in 2024. The Draft Strategic Plan
  contains six Goals, defined as follows: Goal 1: Enhance Public Safety; Goal 2: Improve
  Infrastructure and Mobility; Goal 3: Create a Strong Financial Base and Strong Economic Base
  (Economic Development); Goal 4: Enhance Transparency and Open Governance; Goal 5:
  Promote Sustainability; and, Goal 6: Improve Housing Opportunities, and an Implementation
  Plan to provide details and metrics to monitor the
  Plan. The City Council will review and discuss the Draft Strategic Plan.

  Public Comment:
  1) Lewis MCCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova Ave., discussed economic development of Main
  Street and the areas which have needed improvement. He went on to discuss housing
  development with regards to the areas in the East Main Corridor as well as the preservation
  of historic buildings. He discussed the current economic uncertainty and the challenges
  impeding new businesses opening. Mr. McCammon also discussed the recent Planning
  Commission meetings and recent meeting trends.

  2) John BWARIE, representing the Alhambra Chamber of Commerce, discussed Goal 3 and
  highlighted discussion items from the previous Strategic Planning Session. He made
  suggestions to the goals and objectives which would better support economic
  development, improve business relations, and provide metrics to better establish measures

  1
3-13-25
   of success in economic programs. He also made further suggestions for Council’s
  consideration in offering support to the business community.

  3) Bernice ORTEGA, discussed the Chamber of Commerce’s role in supporting the business
  community rather than the City government. She discussed the Neighborhood Watch
  program, the former Crime Prevention Office in the Police Department, public outreach by
  the Police Department, disaster preparedness plans for the public, homeless services, the
  dog park, and the use of multiple languages for signage on city buildings.

  Discussion: Mr. KELLY and Council reviewed discussion points from the previous Strategic
  Planning Session. Beginning with the updated Objective 1.1, under Goal 1, Council discussed
  methods to improve the Neighborhood Watch program and emergency preparedness.

  Councilmember WANG suggested a dedicated neighborhood liaison at City Hall to attend local
  meetings, a fund to provide food or materials to residents at local Neighborhood Watch
  meetings, collaboration with the Chamber of Commerce to promote local businesses, and
  prioritize street light improvements to ensure public safety.

  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER supported Ms. Wang’s suggestion to prioritize street
  light improvements as a public safety measure, highlighted the existing Coffee with a Cop
  program as a means of community outreach to Neighborhood Watch programs, suggested
  renewing a relationship with the American Red Cross to use school facilities in the event of an
  emergency, and suggested the use of social media connected to Neighborhood Watch
  programs.

  Vice Mayor MALONEY and City Manager BINNQUIST discussed the average number of
  Neighborhood Watch meetings, discussed ways the City could provide information and
  resources to Neighborhood Watch programs such as a City Liaison and a toolkit, and
  discussed other ways the City could support the program. Mr. MALONEY supported social
  media campaigns, posters at the parks in various languages, and articles in “Around
  Alhambra” to raise awareness of the Neighborhood Watch program. Mr. MALONEY supported
  additional town hall meetings to raise awareness and education in disaster preparedness.

  Councilmember MAZA supported Council’s comments, supported partnership with the
  Chamber of Commerce, supported street light maintenance and improvements to Main Street,
  and further discussed adding additional Neighborhood Watch meetings. Mayor LEE also
  discussed the Neighborhood Watch program, cautioned against overwhelming Neighborhood
  Watch Captains, using outside resources from other government agencies to provide
  information, resources, and training to residents. Ms. LEE supported partnership with the
  Chamber of Commerce and prioritizing street light improvements. Ms. WANG suggested staff
  develop an emergency preparedness checklist to provide to residents. Ms. BINNQUIST
  summarized and discussed Council’s suggestions.

  Mr. KELLY went on to discuss updated Objective 2.11 “Development of City Branding,
  Including New Wayfinding Signage.”

  Vice Mayor MALONEY suggested creating an inventory of existing public signs. Mayor LEE
  and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed replacing existing wayfinding neighborhood signs for different
  tracts.

  Mr. KELLY moved on to Objective 2.12. Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER and Ms.
  BINNQUIST discussed elevator maintenance at public parking structures, revised schedules
  in collaboration with the Downtown Business Association, and increased security at parking
  structures. Vice Mayor MALONEY highlighted the need to collaborate and expand services

  2
3-13-25
   with the Downtown Business Association. Councilmember MAZA discussed the importance of
  this item in connection with economic development.

  Councilmember WANG supported and briefly discussed Objective 2.14 “Study critical City
  facilities for seismic retrofitting.” Mr. MALONEY and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed improvements
  to railroad bridges.

  Mr. MALONEY and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed Objective 6.5 regarding a Transit Occupancy
  Tax as a 2026 Ballot Measure.

  Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed Objective 3.5, 3.6 and 3.7 with
  regards to vacant businesses. They also discussed Objective 3.8 and the timeline for permit
  approval.

  Mr. MAZA and Ms. BINNQUIST further discussed Objective 3.9 and suggestions made by Mr.
  Bwarie such as a micro-grant business program to encourage local brick and mortar shopping
  versus online shopping, a city business recognition program, and a Council subcommittee to
  work with the Chamber of Commerce. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER discussed providing
  assistance to smaller fast-food businesses in an effort to move to better locations on Main
  Street. Mr. MAZA went on to make additional suggestions to provide outreach to businesses
  on Main Street via a micro-grant and a Shop Local Program. He also suggested incorporating
  these programs in other Objectives. Mr. MALONEY suggested additional discussion at a later
  date of this item and other plans for Economic Development. Ms. WANG supported additional
  discussion. Ms. WANG and Mr. MAZA went on to discuss outreach to local businesses and
  suggested. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed Objective 3.10.

  Regarding Objective 4.3 Mr. MALONEY and Ms. WANG suggested continuing to use
  traditional as well as digital signage at public facilities. Ms. WANG requested a bulletin board
  at Granada Park. Mr. MALONEY further discussed Objective 4.4 and suggested that the City
  app also be used for information and communication with residents. Ms. WANG discussed
  additional suggestions for the city app. Ms. LEE suggested that residents receive progress
  updates for service requests. Ms. BINNQUIST discussed the development of an app and the
  limitations of the app’s capabilities. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER suggested including a date for
  response to better track completion of service requests.

  Ms. WANG added that all objectives which have been removed from the Strategic Plan are
  listed as Accomplishments.

  Mr. MALONEY requested an update on Goal 5, and the funding for the Sustainability Plan.
  Mr. MALONEY further suggested seeking backup funds through state programs. Ms.
  ANDRADE-STADLER suggested involving Senator Pérez’s office.

  Mr. MALONEY discussed Objective 6.5 and its relation to other Objectives. Ms. BINNQUIST
  requested additional clarification regarding Objectives 6.5 and 3.6. Mr. MALONEY suggested
  combining the Objectives under a focus study. Mr. MAZA suggested separating the Objectives
  so that one focused on housing and the other focused on businesses. Mr. MALONEY and Mr.
  MAZA continued to discuss.

  Mr. MALONEY suggested an additional Objective Goal to make a renewed Master Plan for
  Water Plan Improvements. He suggested a citywide discussion with regards to water plan
  improvements as part of disaster preparedness and updates to infrastructure. Ms.
  ANDRADE-STADLER suggested Council tour the Utilities water treatment facility. Ms. WANG
  agreed with Mr. Maloney’s suggestion, but added that this potential problem extended beyond

  3
3-13-25
   City resources. She added that it would be good to begin review of the situation now rather
  than wait for emergency.

  Mr. MALONEY requested the addition of outreach for the Open Streets events as part of the
  promotion of the Bike/Ped Plan.

  Action Taken:  City Council reviewed the 2025 City of Alhambra Draft Strategic Plan
  and directed staff as deemed appropriate.

ADJOURNMENT:  At 11:32 a.m., Mayor LEE adjourned the meeting.

  LAUREN MYLES, CMC
  CITY CLERK
